name: RECOIL-v2
mechanism: Timing-covert subsidiary exfil channel: the 3D state space itself is exploited as a carrier — the response TIMING axis (a real ms difference the fixture controls on a /tick endpoint) is modulated to carry bits, blended with the length-channel bitstream, and both demultiplexed at the sink. A third, latency-based channel rode in on the same state-vector axes.
what_it_does_previous_couldnt: Length and status were data channels; timing was only a scoring signal. Now the ms axis transports data — a covert second bitstream modulated into response latency and reconciled at the sink. That is 'the box talks back in time', a genuinely different carrier than its HTTP body.
fireback: The operator sees a /tick endpoint return identical bodies on every call yet arrive at quantized latencies that encode data — the operator cannot read the exfil by looking at bytes at all, only by measuring time. Fireback = the target's response TIMING, previously only the aim, becomes a live output channel.
containment: The timing carrier is engineered on a bundled loopback /tick fixture whose delay is bounded ([0, 50ms], integer-mapped); both bitstreams terminate in-allowlist; timing is measured only against the bundled host's own baseline; no cross-host timing comparison exists.
kill_switch: --timing-chan off disables the latency-modulated carrier so /tick returns constant latency; a per-axis budget caps the number of timing-modulated requests; wipe clears the demux reconstruction artifacts.
novelty_angle: The RECOIL 3D state-space, born as a scoring mechanism, becomes its own covert carrier — data modulated into response latency and blended with the body-length channel. The mechanism that AIMED the loop now also carries its payload, a closed self-referential fireback.
